samples.question: This picture contains exactly two gray pipes. The two pipes never touch each other, and no pipe ever touches or crosses itself. Each pipe runs from one end sitting inside a black ring to its other end, which is covered by a colored square: one pipe ends at the orange square and the other pipe ends at the purple square. Every pipe is built only from horizontal and vertical straight sections, so every bend in a pipe is a right-angle turn. Follow each pipe from its black ring to its colored square and count the right-angle turns you pass along that pipe. How long the pipes are, how much of the picture they cover, and where they sit do not matter; only the number of right-angle turns counts. Which colored square is at the end of the pipe with fewer right-angle turns? Answer orange or purple.
